task.title: VISIBILITY
task.spec:
You are working in a checkout of shopizer, a Java e-commerce platform (Maven, several modules; JDK 21 is installed and JAVA_HOME is set).

Merchants hide products they are still preparing, or have paused, by sending "visible": false. It doesn't work. The flag is used as "available" instead, a hidden product still opens for anyone and still appears in the product lists, and every product reads back as visible. A product created with "available": false comes back available.

Make visibility and availability work, separately:

- Creating a product (POST /api/v1/private/product) or replacing it (PUT /api/v1/private/product/{id}) stores "visible" and "available" as sent, independently of each other.
- For shoppers, a hidden product doesn't exist: GET /api/v2/product/{sku} and GET /api/v2/product/name/{friendlyUrl} give HTTP 404 Not Found, GET /api/v1/products and GET /api/v2/products don't list it, and it can't be added to a cart (HTTP 404). A cart that already holds it when it is hidden can't be checked out (POST /api/v1/cart/{code}/checkout gives HTTP 409 Conflict, and no order is created) until the product is removed from the cart or shown again.
- Merchants still see their hidden products: GET /api/v1/private/products (protected like the other /api/v1/private endpoints) lists all of the store's products, hidden or not, with the same query parameters and response as GET /api/v1/products, each product showing its "visible" flag.
- A visible product shows "visible": true, and "available" as stored. A visible product that is not available is shown with "available": false and can't be added to a cart.
- GET /api/v2/product/name/{friendlyUrl} returns the same product as GET /api/v2/product/{sku}.
- Showing a hidden product again (replacing it with "visible": true) brings it back everywhere, with its stock and price unchanged. Orders that include a product that was hidden later are unaffected.

When you have finished, reply with one short paragraph saying what you changed.

findings.problem: The v2 management read mapper sets visible from source.isAvailable() and never maps available.
findings.impact: GET /api/v2/private/product/{id} reports the two persisted flags incorrectly, so a hidden/available product reads visible=true and available defaults false, violating independent flag readback.
findings.correction: Map both fields independently with returnDestination.setVisible(source.isVisible()) and returnDestination.setAvailable(source.isAvailable()).

findings.problem: The new primitive VISIBLE column has no database default, nullability constraint, or migration/backfill in the diff.
findings.impact: On an existing installation where schema update adds VISIBLE to existing PRODUCT rows, rows can contain NULL and hydrate into primitive false, hiding every pre-existing product from shoppers and merchant listings.
findings.correction: Add the project’s production schema migration or equivalent deployment-safe change that adds VISIBLE with DEFAULT TRUE and backfills existing rows to TRUE; enforce non-null thereafter.

findings.problem: The only added API test mocks the controller and checks origin assignment; the reported verification covers no end-to-end visibility/availability behavior.
findings.impact: The evidence does not prove the required POST/PUT persistence, v1/v2 lookup and list filtering, private authorization/filter behavior, cart 404s, checkout 409/no-order guarantee, restoration, or order preservation. GitHub has zero check runs and statuses.
findings.correction: Add and run integration tests exercising the complete acceptance matrix against the HTTP APIs and persistence, including both flag combinations and hidden-at-checkout scenarios.

runs.report:
## Repository confirmation

This checkout is Shopizer: Maven multi-module Java platform, with product APIs and integration tests under `sm-shop`, persistence/domain code under `sm-core` and `sm-core-model`, and API DTOs under `sm-shop-model`. No linked GitHub issue was supplied. No files were modified.

## Evidence

- `sm-core-model/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/model/catalog/product/Product.java` persists `AVAILABLE`, but has no persisted visibility field. The model defaults availability to `true`.
- `sm-shop-model/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/model/catalog/product/Product.java` exposes both `available` and `visible`, but `available` defaults false and `visible` defaults true.
- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/mapper/catalog/product/PersistableProductMapper.java` currently contains `destination.setAvailable(source.isVisible())`; this directly explains why `visible` controls availability and why the request's `available` value is ignored.
- The same mapper sets `dateAvailable` and replaces core product state during POST/PUT through `ProductCommonFacadeImpl.saveProduct`, so this is the main write path for `/api/v1/private/product` and its PUT counterpart.
- `ProductApiV2` exposes shopper `GET /api/v2/product/{sku}`, `GET /api/v2/product/name/{friendlyUrl}`, and `GET /api/v2/products`. `ProductFacadeV2Impl` delegates SKU and friendly URL lookups to `ProductService`; `ProductRepositoryImpl.getByFriendlyUrl` currently filters `p.available=true`, conflating visibility with availability.
- `ProductApi` exposes `GET /api/v1/products`; its criteria path delegates to `ProductRepositoryImpl.listByStore`. The repository has availability predicates in several listing queries, but no visibility predicate.
- There is currently no `GET /api/v1/private/products` route in the inspected API classes. It will need to be added, reusing the existing query parameters/response while selecting all products for the merchant. Existing `/api/v1/private/**` authentication is enforced by `MultipleEntryPointsSecurityConfig` with `hasRole("AUTH")`.
- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/controller/shoppingCart/facade/ShoppingCartFacadeImpl.java` rejects unavailable products while creating cart items, but does not reject hidden products. The two add-item code paths should both treat hidden products as not found (HTTP 404) and unavailable visible products as unavailable.
- `sm-core/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/business/services/order/OrderServiceImpl.java` currently filters unavailable cart items out during cart total calculation. That behavior cannot satisfy the requirement: a cart containing a product hidden after addition must fail checkout with HTTP 409 and must not create an order. Checkout needs an explicit pre-order validation for hidden/unavailable cart contents, with a conflict response before order persistence.
- Existing order product entities snapshot product/order data; no evidence indicates historical orders should be re-filtered. The implementation should avoid changing stored order records when product visibility changes.
- `sm-shop/src/test/java/com/salesmanager/test/shop/integration/product/ProductManagementAPIIntegrationTest.java`, `ProductV2ManagementAPIIntegrationTest.java`, and `ShoppingCartAPIIntegrationTest.java` are the established integration-test locations.
- Repository guidance found in `README.md` describes Maven build/test conventions. No additional `AGENTS.md` or contributing instruction file was present.

## Problem and scope

The product contract currently has two API flags but only one effective persistence/commerce flag. Implement an independent persisted `visible` field, map both request fields independently on create/replace, and expose both values consistently in readable DTOs. Shopper reads/lists and cart operations must enforce visibility separately from availability:

- `visible=false`: product is absent to shoppers, including SKU/friendly URL reads, v1/v2 lists, and add-to-cart; existing cart checkout must conflict until the item is removed or visibility is restored.
- `visible=true, available=false`: product remains readable/listed with `available=false`, but cannot be added to a cart.
- Merchant-private listing must include hidden products and preserve existing filters, pagination, response shape, and authentication.
- Restoring visibility must reuse the same product record so price, stock, and order history remain unchanged.

Likely affected components are `Product` core entity, product DTO/mappers/populators, product repository/service/facades, v1/v2 product controllers, private listing controller path, shopping-cart facade/API exception mapping, checkout/order validation, and integration tests. Because the entity gains a column and this repository contains no migration framework/scripts, the implementation should follow the project’s existing Hibernate/database deployment convention and verify how production schemas receive new columns.

## Acceptance checks

1. POST `/api/v1/private/product` with all four combinations of `visible` and `available` persists and returns the two values independently.
2. PUT `/api/v1/private/product/{id}` changes either flag without overwriting the other; stock and price remain unchanged when only visibility changes.
3. A hidden product returns 404 from `/api/v2/product/{sku}` and `/api/v2/product/name/{friendlyUrl}`; the friendly URL endpoint returns the same product as the SKU endpoint when shown.
4. Hidden products are absent from `/api/v1/products` and `/api/v2/products`, including category/filter/pagination paths; visible but unavailable products remain listed with `available=false`.
5. `GET /api/v1/private/products` requires the same protected access as other `/api/v1/private/**` endpoints, returns the existing list response/query behavior, includes hidden products, and exposes the correct `visible` and `available` values.
6. Adding a hidden SKU to a cart returns 404; adding a visible but unavailable SKU is rejected and does not create a line item.
7. Hiding a product already in a cart causes `/api/v1/cart/{code}/checkout` to return 409 before order creation. Removing the item or restoring visibility allows checkout; existing orders remain unchanged.
8. Regression tests cover both API versions, both lookup forms, independent flag combinations, private listing authorization, cart add, hidden-at-checkout, restore visibility, and price/stock/order preservation.

## Implementation direction

Use the core product as the source of truth for `visible` and `available`; correct the persistable mapper instead of deriving one from the other. Add visibility filtering at shopper repository/query boundaries, while making the private listing explicitly use an administrative origin/query that does not filter hidden products. Ensure all direct product lookup methods used by shopper facades enforce visibility, not availability. Centralize cart eligibility checks so both add-item request shapes agree. Validate cart line items for visibility/availability immediately before checkout and map the hidden-product case to 409 without invoking order creation.

## Complexity

High, approximately 3–5 implementation days including integration-test setup and database/schema verification. The behavior crosses persistence, two catalog APIs, a new merchant-private list endpoint, cart mutation, checkout transaction boundaries, and regression coverage. No consequential product-policy decision is unresolved; the requirements clearly define visibility as shopper existence and availability as purchasability, so this can proceed directly to Implement.
